message.content:
Here's a comprehensive step-by-step guide to setting up a new router for WiFi access:

## What You'll Need
- Your new router and power adapter
- An Ethernet cable (usually included)
- Your modem (from your internet provider)
- A computer or smartphone
- Your ISP login credentials (if required for PPPoE connection)

---

## Step 1: Choose the Right Location
Place your router in a **central, elevated location** away from:
- Metal objects and appliances
- Microwaves and cordless phones
- Corners, cabinets, or enclosed spaces

Good placement ensures better signal coverage throughout your home.

---

## Step 2: Connect the Hardware

1. **Unplug or turn off your modem** (cable/DSL/fiber)
2. **Connect the modem to the router**: Use an Ethernet cable to connect your modem's LAN port to the router's **WAN/Internet port**
3. **Attach antennas** (if your router has external ones)
4. **Plug in the power adapter** and turn on the router
5. **Turn your modem back on** and wait 2-3 minutes for both devices to fully boot up

---

## Step 3: Connect to Your Router

You have two options:

**Option A - WiFi:**
- Find the default WiFi network name (SSID) and password on the label/sticker on your router
- Connect your computer or phone to this network

**Option B - Ethernet (more stable for setup):**
- Connect an Ethernet cable from your computer to one of the router's LAN ports

---

## Step 4: Access the Router's Admin Panel

1. Open a web browser
2. Enter the router's default IP address in the address bar:
   - Common addresses: `192.168.1.1` or `192.168.0.1`
   - Some brands use: `http://router.asus.com` or similar
3. Enter the default login credentials (found on the router label):
   - Common defaults: Username `admin`, Password `admin` or `password`

> **Tip:** Check your router's manual or label for the exact IP and credentials for your model.

---

## Step 5: Run the Setup Wizard

Most routers will launch an automatic setup wizard. Follow the prompts to:

### Configure Internet Connection
Select your connection type:
| Type | When to Use |
|------|-------------|
| **Dynamic IP (DHCP)** | Most cable internet users; no login credentials needed |
| **PPPoE** | DSL users; requires username/password from your ISP |
| **Static IP** | Your ISP provided fixed IP settings |

You can usually click **"Auto Detect"** if unsure.

---

## Step 6: Configure Your WiFi Network

This is the most important step for security:

1. **Change the SSID (WiFi name)**: Choose a unique name you'll recognize
2. **Set a strong WiFi password**: Use at least 12 characters with a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
3. **Select security type**: Choose **WPA2** or **WPA3** (never use WEP or open network)
4. **Configure both bands** (if dual-band):
   - 2.4 GHz: Better range, slower speeds
   - 5 GHz: Faster speeds, shorter range

---

## Step 7: Change the Admin Password

Immediately change the default router administrator password to prevent unauthorized access to your settings. This is usually found under **System** or **Administration** settings.

---

## Step 8: Update Firmware

Check for firmware updates in the router settings (usually under **System Tools** or **Firmware Update**). Installing updates improves performance, adds features, and patches security vulnerabilities.

---

## Step 9: Apply Advanced Security Settings (Recommended)

| Setting | Recommendation |
|---------|---------------|
| **Disable Remote Access** | Turn off "Remote Administration" or "Web Access from WAN" |
| **Enable Firewall** | Keep the built-in firewall enabled |
| **Set up Guest Network** | Create a separate network for visitors |
| **Consider DNS change** | Use Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Google (8.8.8.8) for better privacy |

---

## Step 10: Save and Test

1. Click **Save** or **Apply** to confirm all changes
2. Wait for the router to restart (if prompted)
3. Reconnect your devices using the **new WiFi name and password**
4. Test your internet connection by browsing websites or running a speed test

---

## Troubleshooting Tips

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Can't access admin page | Verify you're connected to the router; try a different browser; clear cache |
| No internet connection | Check modem-to-router cable; power cycle both devices; verify ISP settings |
| Weak WiFi signal | Relocate router to a more central, elevated position |
| Forgot admin password | Press and hold the router's reset button for 10-30 seconds to factory reset |

---

## Alternative: Use Manufacturer's Mobile App

Many brands (NETGEAR Nighthawk, TP-Link Tether, ASUS Router, etc.) offer mobile apps that simplify setup:
1. Download the app
2. Scan the QR code on your router
3. Follow the guided instructions

---

Sources:
1. https://kb.netgear.com/119/Setting-up-and-installing-your-NETGEAR-router
2. https://www.tp-link.com/us/support/faq/3841/
3. https://www.actcorp.in/blog/how-to-configure-router
4. https://huasifei-link.com/how-to-set-up-5g-sim-card-wifi-router-home-internet/
5. https://wifitech.ae/how-to-configure-router/
6. https://www.fwweekly.com/2025/06/27/how-to-set-up-a-new-wifi-router-like-a-pro/
7. https://www.eolo.it/blog/guide-tech/configurare-router-wifi
8. http://product.pconline.com.cn/itbk/top/qa/1863/18635638.html
